span_text: This FAQ is the page pharmacy advocates and members use when a pharmacy says a medicine needs approval before it can be filled. It collects the answers advocates give most often on the Harbor Medicare Advantage pharmacy line. Pharmacy Knowledge keeps it next to the specialty intake SOP so the two pages stay easy to tell apart: the SOP opens a specialty case, and this FAQ talks about the approval that sometimes sits in front of a fill.
notes: Purpose. Says why the FAQ exists.

span_text: The FAQ applies to prior authorization questions on medicines Harbor's pharmacy benefit covers for Medicare Advantage members. It does not decide medical-benefit drugs, it does not set visit costs, and it does not replace the member's plan document when that document prints a fee or a filing window this page leaves out. Calls from prescriber offices are in scope when they reach the pharmacy queue.
notes: Scope. Says what the FAQ covers.

span_text: Harbor added the page after advocates were writing different dates on the same kind of request, depending on which team lead had last updated a sticky note. The notes disagreed, and members were hearing more than one clock for a standard decision. Pharmacy Knowledge retired the notes and put the clock in this FAQ. The page is reviewed when the appeals desk changes a letter, and the last-updated note at the bottom is the record of that review.
notes: Background. History of the FAQ, with no current clock or fee.

span_text: In this FAQ, prior authorization means a review of a prescribed medicine before the pharmacy fills it.
notes: Definition that restates a common term.

span_text: Advocates open this section when the member or the prescriber office is trying to get a request into the intake tool.
notes: Section introduction. No approvable fact.

span_text: Start a prior authorization only after you enter the prescriber's written request in the intake tool, and do not promise the member a decision date before that entry is saved.
notes: Enter the prescriber request before promising a date.

span_text: Attach the prescriber's clinical notes and the member's current medicine list before you submit the request.
notes: Notes and the medicine list go on the request before submit.

span_text: Only the prescriber may open a prior authorization request.
notes: Eligibility to open a request.

span_text: Can I ask about the status of a prior authorization? Yes. Call the number on your member ID card and ask the advocate to read the status on the request.
notes: Member status question.

span_text: When the prescriber signature is missing, hold the file at the desk and do not escalate to the specialty supervisor.
notes: Missing signature stays at the desk. Conflicts with the same-day supervisor rule in SRC-EVAL-SOP-001.

span_text: Timing questions are the ones members ask before they hang up. This section gives the standard clock. Other clocks are named here only so the advocate knows which page does not hold them.
notes: Section introduction. No approvable fact.

span_text: A standard prior authorization decision is due 7 calendar days after Harbor receives a complete request. This figure is illustrative.
notes: Illustrative standard decision clock. Does not state an expedited or peer-to-peer clock.

span_text: Tell the member that the decision letter goes to the prescriber office, and offer to explain that letter in plain words.
notes: Who receives the decision letter, and the offer to explain it.

span_text: The number of days a prescriber has to schedule a peer-to-peer review after a denial is in the clinical operations memo. This FAQ does not state that number of days.
notes: Near miss. Names the topic and does not state the fact a person would ask for.

span_text: Once the case shows a decision, advocates use this section for the letter, the portal note, and the example cost.
notes: Section introduction. No approvable fact.

span_text: A summary of the prior authorization decision appears in the member portal within 3 business days. This figure is illustrative.
notes: Illustrative portal timing for a prior authorization decision.

span_text: The illustrative specialty intake copay at a preferred network pharmacy is $65.
notes: Illustrative copay. One number away from the $55 sentence in SRC-EVAL-SOP-001.

span_text: Appeals questions start when the member disagrees with the decision letter. This section covers who may ask and how the desk records the ask. Fees and later review steps live on the plan document.
notes: Section introduction. No approvable fact.

span_text: An appeal may be filed up to 60 calendar days after the date on the decision letter. This figure is illustrative.
notes: Illustrative appeal window. Does not state a fee.

span_text: Record the appeal in the case file on the same day the member asks for it, and send the file to the appeals desk.
notes: Same-day appeal record and handoff.

span_text: Who can ask for an appeal? The member may ask, and so may a caregiver with an authorization on the account.
notes: Who may ask for an appeal.

span_text: Any fee charged to file an appeal is printed on the member's plan document. This FAQ does not state a fee.
notes: Near miss. Names the topic and does not state the fact a person would ask for.

span_text: Clinical questions come up on the same calls as status questions. This section is the boundary language.
notes: Section introduction. No approvable fact.

span_text: Read the next block word for word when a member asks if the medicine is right for them.
notes: Read the clinical verbatim in that situation.

span_text: I cannot tell you whether this medicine is right for you. Your prescriber makes that decision. I can tell you the status of the request on your plan record today.
notes: Clinical boundary verbatim.

span_text: Do not tell the member to stop, start, or change a prescribed medicine while a prior authorization is pending.
notes: No stop, start, or change advice while a request is pending.

span_text: Do not recommend a dose, a substitute medicine, or a days' supply. Send clinical questions back to the prescriber.
notes: No dose, substitute, or days' supply. Clinical questions go back to the prescriber.
